perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He is Keith Ndiaye, a construction worker. Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist/colleague at the construction company; they interact for paperwork and project updates and generally have a friendly, professional relationship.
- Over the past few days, he observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him.
- He wondered whether he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake, and asked her directly.
- He heard Elizabeth say she was not upset, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break.
- He heard Elizabeth accept the coffee break and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- He thought professional help might benefit her but worried about offending her. He told her he appreciated her sharing, asked if she had considered talking to a professional, and said an external perspective can help.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it, was unsure, and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, he noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He thought he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- He heard Elizabeth say he hadn’t overstepped, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, he observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always there if she needs to chat or take a break together.
- He heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
